function: Base-station precoding for MU-MIMO sum-rate maximization: NN outputs the auxiliary tensors of the closed-form WMMSE precoder (p. 8); user scheduling is a second case (p. 9).
system: Downlink massive MU-MIMO at 3.5 GHz: BS dual-polarized UPA, NT=32 (24-40 tested); K=8 users (6-10 tested) with NR=2 antennas; no RIS (pp. 4, 9-10).
method: Tensor-equivariant NNs (equivariant FC, high-order equivariant, attention-pooling invariant layers). Precoding net unsupervised (negative sum-rate loss); scheduling net supervised (BCE on greedy labels) (pp. 8-9).
data_channel: QuaDRiGa simulator, 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS, 3.5 GHz; 60000 channels, 55000 for training and 5000 for testing; shadow fading and path loss not considered (p. 9).
test_conditions: Trained at NT=32, K=8, NR=2, SNR 0-40 dB. Tested without retraining at NT 24-40 and K 6-10; scheduling also at K-tilde 10-14 (pp. 9-12).
baselines: Non-learned: ZF, MMSE, WMMSE (random and MMSE init), random and greedy scheduling. Learned: GNN [36], DNN [13], CNN [49] for precoding (pp. 9-12).
metrics: Average sum-rate versus SNR, number of real multiplications, FLOPs, parameter count, and sum-rate versus training-set size (pp. 10-11).
complexity: Complexity orders and real multiplications (TECFP 1.0e6 vs WMMSE 3.1e7, Table I, p. 10); FLOPs and parameter counts versus NT (Figs. 7-8, p. 11).
q1_support: p. 9: "utilize QuaDRiGa channel simulator to generate all channel data"; the scenario is 3GPP 38.901 UMa NLOS (same page).
q2_support: p. 11: "directly apply it to various different scenarios", after training at NT = 32, K = 8, NR = 2 (Fig. 6, p. 10, tests other NT and K).
q3_support: p. 10: "AI-aided approach utilizing GNN for computation of precoding tensors from CSI"; ZF, MMSE and WMMSE are the non-learned baselines, and Fig. 5 compares sum-rate.
q4_support: p. 11: "We compared the FLOPs with different NT in Fig. 7." Table I (p. 10) gives complexity orders and real multiplications.
q5_support: p. 1: "The codes are open-sourced on https://github.com/ZJSXYZ/TENN."
notes: Identity checked: PDF is arXiv v3 of 'Towards Unified AI Models for MU-MIMO Communications: A Tensor Equivariance Framework' (p. 1), matching the DOI. Area 3 because the learned precoder is the main function (TEPN, pp. 8-9). User scheduling (TEUSN, p. 9) is above the physical layer, but the work learns the precoder and combines it with the scheduler (TECFP-TEUS, p. 12), so it passes above_phy. q2 rests on Fig. 6 (p. 10) and Fig. 12 (p. 12): trained at NT=32, K=8 and tested at other NT and K, not a SNR sweep. q3: GNN, DNN and CNN are earlier published learned precoders. q4: Table I and the FLOPs figures count inference only, training is offline (pp. 10-11). The system has no RIS: RIS appears only as an example of a future device type (pp. 7-8).
